tools.name: upload_file_to_spo
tools.description:
Uploads a local file to a specified path in SharePoint Online (SPO).

Args:
    site_url (str): The URL of the SharePoint Online site, e.g., 'https://yourcompany.sharepoint.com/sites/YourSite'.
    file_path (str): The full path to the local file, e.g., 'C:/Users/user/Documents/report.pdf'.
    spo_path (str): The relative path to the target folder in SharePoint Online.
                    Example: 'Shared Documents/04_FRDC技術支援（AI関連）/08_2024/04_Traffic LLM datalabeling/99_納品'
                    This path is relative to the site's root or a document library.

Returns:
    str: The upload result message.

tools.name: get_list_data
tools.description:
Retrieves data from a specified SharePoint Online (SPO) list and saves it as a local JSON file.

Args:
    site_url (str): The URL of the SharePoint Online site, e.g., 'https://yourcompany.sharepoint.com/sites/YourSite'.
    list_id (str, optional): The GUID (Globally Unique Identifier) of the SharePoint list.
                             Example: '{{A1B2C3D4-E5F6-7890-1234-567890ABCDEF}}'.
                             Mutually exclusive with `list_name`; only one should be provided.
    list_name (str, optional): The display name of the SharePoint list.
                               Example: 'My Custom List'.
                               Mutually exclusive with `list_id`; only one should be provided.
    fields (list[str], optional): A list of field names to retrieve. If None or empty, all fields are retrieved.
                                  Example: ['Title', 'Author', 'Created'].
    query (dict[str, str], optional): A dictionary representing the query conditions.
                                      Keys are field names, and values are the desired values to match.
                                      Example: {'Status': 'Completed', 'Priority': 'High'}.
                                      Note: This simple dictionary query currently only supports 'Eq' (equals) operations.
                                      For more complex queries, the internal logic would need to be expanded.
    op (str, optional): The logical operator to combine multiple query conditions.
                        Currently supports "And" or "Or". Defaults to "And".

Returns:
    str: The full path to the temporary JSON file where the list data is saved.

tools.name: upload_and_vectorize_document
tools.description:
Upload a local document into a vector knowledge base and vectorize it.

The file is read from disk and sent to the MooFile upload endpoint, then
a vectorization task is started for it. When `wait` is True the tool polls
the task until it finishes and reports the final state and chunk count.

local_path.description:
Absolute path of the document file on this machine.
Supported extensions (parseable by the backend worker): .txt, .md,
.markdown, .csv, .html, .htm, .json, .log.

db_id.description: The target knowledge base id; it must be a vector knowledge base.

chunk_size.description: Target chunk size in characters (100-2000, default 500).

overlap.description: Chunk overlap in characters (0 <= overlap < chunk_size, default 20).

model.description: Embedding model name; leave empty to use the knowledge base default.

wait.description: If True (default), block until the vectorization task completes.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait for the task (default 600).

tools.name: retrieve_knowledge
tools.description:
Semantic search over a vector knowledge base (RAG retrieval).

The query is embedded with the knowledge base's configured model and the
most similar chunks are returned. Omitting top_k / threshold makes the
backend fall back to the knowledge base's vectorConfig defaults.

top_k.description:
Max number of results (use 0 to fall back to the database
default, normally 10).

threshold.description:
Minimum similarity score to keep a result, 0-1
(use -1 to fall back to the database default, normally 0.3).

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.title: Browser Screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of the current (most recently opened) page.

page_index.description: Which page to capture. -1 means the most recent page.

full_page.description:
Whether to capture the full scrollable page (True) or only
the visible viewport (False).

tools.name: browser_get_content
tools.title: Browser Get Content
tools.description: Extract the current page content in a model-friendly form.

format.description:
One of "text" (readable page text), "html" (raw page HTML), or
"xml" (a simplified XML element tree). The XML tree annotates every
element with its key attributes and a `css="..."` selector path so
it can be used directly to locate elements for click/fill actions.

max_length.description: Maximum characters returned for text/html output.

max_depth.description: Maximum DOM depth in the XML element tree.

max_nodes.description: Maximum number of elements in the XML element tree.

page_index.description: Which page to read. -1 means the most recent page.

tools.name: browser_execute_js
tools.title: Browser Execute Js
tools.description:
Execute JavaScript in the current page and return its result.

Use this to verify elements before acting on them: check that a selector
matches, read an element's state, or extract a value (e.g.
``document.querySelector('#submit') !== null``,
``document.querySelectorAll('.item').length``). The result is returned as
JSON when it is structured, otherwise as its string form.

script.description:
JavaScript expression to evaluate in the page's main frame.
For multi-statement logic wrap it in an IIFE, e.g.
``(function(){ var el = document.querySelector('#x'); return el ? el.value : null; })()``.

page_index.description: Which page to run on. -1 means the most recent page.

tools.name: do_automation_by_script
tools.title: Do Automation By Script
tools.description:
Execute browser automation steps from a JSON script file.

The JSON file must contain a list of step lists. Each step list is passed to
the browser automation runner, which supports navigation, interaction,
waiting, text extraction, and screenshots. ``wait_user`` controls
visibility: True shows the browser window, False runs it headless.

The browser stays resident after the call on purpose, so later tool calls
(browser_screenshot / browser_get_content / further automation) reuse the
same instance instead of relaunching Edge. It is torn down when this MCP
process exits.

script_param_file.description: Path to the UTF-8 encoded JSON automation script. Sample file placed in the ./samples folder.

wait_user.description: Whether to show the browser window (True) or run headless (False).
